agents.agent_name: Business Logic + File Upload Testing Agent
agents.task: Test business logic flaws and file upload vulnerabilities on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on: (1) Race conditions in purchases or checkout, (2) Price manipulation, quantity manipulation, (3) Order/payment workflow bypass, (4) File upload bypass (extension, content-type, magic bytes), (5) Path traversal in file operations, (6) Coupon/discount abuse, (7) State machine violations. Build working PoCs for any confirmed vulnerabilities. Report findings to root agent.

Perform exhaustive reconnaissance on http://host.docker.internal:3100. This is OWASP Juice Shop, a deliberately vulnerable web app. Your goal: discover ALL endpoints, parameters, technologies, authentication flows, and user roles. Use the proxy, crawl thoroughly (both unauthenticated and authenticated if possible), extract API endpoints from JavaScript, and enumerate all discoverable surfaces. Document findings in notes so other agents can use them. Do NOT test for vulnerabilities yet—only map the attack surface.

Test SQL injection and authentication bypass vectors on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on: (1) login form SQLi, (2) search/filter parameter SQLi, (3) API endpoints accepting user input, (4) authentication bypass in login/reset flows, (5) JWT weaknesses (if present). Use sqlmap for injection testing where applicable. Build working PoCs for any confirmed vulnerabilities. Do NOT test other classes yet (XSS, IDOR, etc.)—stay focused on SQLi and auth. Report findings to the root agent.

Test XSS and IDOR vulnerabilities on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on: (1) Reflected XSS in search, parameters, URL fragments, (2) Stored XSS in product reviews, user profiles, comments, (3) DOM-based XSS in Angular components, (4) IDOR in user profiles, orders, reviews, and other object references, (5) Horizontal/vertical privilege escalation through parameter tampering. Build working PoCs for any confirmed vulnerabilities. Coordinate with other agents to avoid overlap. Report findings to root agent.

entries.evidence: Confirmed SQL injection vulnerability in email parameter. Payload ' OR 1=1-- successfully bypasses authentication and returns valid JWT token for admin user. Report: vuln-0001
Confirmed boolean-based SQL injection in search parameter. Payload ' OR '1'='1 returns all 46 products instead of search results. Report: vuln-0002
SQL injection enables authentication bypass. Covered in vuln-0001.
JWT uses RS256 (asymmetric, appropriate). No alg=none, no HS256, no JWKS header injection observed. Token verification successful on API endpoints. No weaknesses found in JWT implementation itself.
Tested registration endpoint with SQLi payloads in email and username fields. All payloads returned 500 status code without processing. No successful SQLi demonstrated.
Tested password reset endpoint with SQLi payloads. All requests returned 500 status. No successful exploitation found.
Tested API endpoints with SQLi payloads in query parameters. All requests returned 200 status with expected results. No SQL error messages or unexpected behavior observed.
Unauthenticated PUT requests return 200 OK and persist product modifications. Tested by updating product description and verifying changes via subsequent GET request.
XSS payloads are reflected in error page title tags. Example: GET /rest/search?q=%3Csvg%20onload%3Dalert(1)%3E returns 500 error with payload in title tag
Public product catalog is accessible without authentication. This is expected behavior for e-commerce application. No sensitive information exposed beyond public product data.
Product reviews are public and accessible without authentication. This is expected behavior for e-commerce application.
DELETE requests return 401 Unauthorized, requiring authentication. This endpoint is properly protected.
User registration endpoint properly accepts unauthenticated requests (expected behavior). No authorization bypass found.
